newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip, seen to edge down further.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip, seen to edge down further.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped on Friday on weak Western interest and thin trading volumes, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 0.67 percent to 173.08 on $10.21 million in trade volume.
Traders forecast the market would continue edging down until President Boris Yeltsin underwent his heart operation, scheduled for the end of September.
"I expect a smooth glide down until the president undergoes his operation and over the month of his recovery," said Ilya Galtsov, a trader from Trinfiko brokerage.

Gazprom was one of the gainers of the day, with prices rising to $0.333 from $0.325 at Thursday's close on news that the company plans to place depositary receipts in early October on the London Stock Exchange, Galtsov said.
UES edged up on news that the government would sell its 7.5 percent stake in the electricity utility through an issue of convertible bonds.
"There was some splash of activity after the announcement and the price started moving more actively," said German Zvezdin, a trader from Troika-Dialog.
St Petersburg Telephone edged up late in the day to $22.00 from $21.50, as investors contemplated a forthcoming auction of a 1.2 percent state stake in the firm on October 9, Galtsov said.
LUKoil was flat at $9.55 after $9.56, Mosenergo slipped to $0.938 from $0.944 and Irkutskenergo was steady at $0.101 from $0.102.
